scenarios.title: Golden path
scenarios.desc: From a blank state: onboard both devices, pair the tablet, bank a message, jump to bedtime, watch it arrive and play, see 'watched' on the guardian phone.

steps.cap: Both devices start blank. The first question on each is role first: who is using this device?
On Jess’s phone, pick Mom.
She confirms her name and label.
Next, the child: name and age. The age locks once setup finishes.
Home time zone, so the app can show “hers” and “yours” side by side.
A four-digit PIN, typed twice. It guards pairing codes.
Connect this device is the last step, because it needs the internet. This creates the family on the (simulated) server.
Now the tablet. A grown-up makes a pairing code; the PIN is required and a child can never make one.
On Ivy’s tablet the same question comes first. She picks Kid.
She types her name.
She picks her age, then locks it. It cannot be changed from the tablet.
A colour and a birthday.
What does she call her grown-ups? Like contacts. This belongs to her; a guardian can never overwrite it.
Connect this device is LAST. Her answers are already saved on the tablet. She types the 6-digit code from the phone.
Paired. Her draft answers upload now, and the tablet is locked in to the app.
Back on the guardian phone, Home now shows one sentence about her state and the two clocks.
Jess banks a goodnight message. Banking means: recorded now, delivered later, when Ivy can actually receive it.
Nothing reaches the tablet yet. The delivery worker waits for bedtime on Ivy’s side of the clock. Let us jump the virtual clock to her bedtime.
It arrives on the tablet as a picture, not a number. She opens it.
She watches it all the way through. Only a full play counts as “watched”.
Back on the guardian phone: Watched. Delivered, opened and watched are three different facts.

scenarios.title: Offline night
scenarios.desc: The tablet loses its network at night. The message is safe on the server and arrives when the tablet is back.

steps.cap: A ready family. Jess banks a message for tonight.
Ivy’s tablet goes offline (flat battery, bad wifi, a road trip). The guardian phone stays online.
Bedtime arrives. The server tries to deliver; the tablet cannot receive it. The guardian sees an honest status, not a false “delivered”.
On the tablet the offline state is a picture, with no error code and no counts.
The network returns. The tablet checks in and the message arrives.
Nothing was lost and nothing was sent twice.

scenarios.title: Birthday band change
scenarios.desc: Ivy turns 13 at local midnight. The age increments and the child home changes shape.

steps.cap: Ivy is 12. The tablet shows the 8 to 12 layout.
Her birthday is tomorrow. Let us jump the virtual clock to local midnight.
She is 13. The age band moved to 13 to 17, and the home re-lays itself out on its own. No badge, no reward, no confetti count (prohibitions P1 to P3).
The console slider shows the derived band. Drag it to see every band live.

scenarios.title: Call knock
scenarios.desc: Ivy knocks to call a grown-up; the guardian phone rings and answers. A child can never start a call the other way round.

steps.cap: Ivy taps the picture of Mom to knock. A knock is not a call: it asks, it does not ring.
On Jess’s phone the knock shows up and it rings.
Jess answers.
They talk. A child tablet has no way to place a call at the guardian; guardians call, children knock.
Jess ends the call.

scenarios.title: Play window
scenarios.desc: A guardian sets a play window; the tablet's games wind down and rest on schedule, then open again in the morning.

steps.cap: Jess opens Play window and daily time. Times are in Ivy’s time zone, not hers.
She turns the window on and picks when games open and rest, with a gentle wind-down.
Saved. A longer window would tell the other guardian; a shorter one never does.
On the tablet the games are open right now. Nothing counts down, and there is no timer on screen.
Jump to the start of the wind-down (15 minutes before rest). A game in progress can finish; new ones wait.
Rest time. The games tile goes quiet, with a moon, and a plain picture tells her why.
Next morning, at 7:30, the window opens again by itself.

scenarios.title: Family change released
scenarios.desc: A guardian saves a change to Ivy's people but holds it until she has been told; releasing it updates her tablet.

steps.cap: Jess opens Family structure: Ivy’s people and homes.
She adds Grandma Rose and chooses to HOLD the change until she has told Ivy. Nothing reaches the tablet yet.
The history shows the change as held. Marcus is told the same day. Nothing has changed on Ivy’s side.
Ivy’s tablet is unchanged: no badge, no surprise.
Jess has had the talk with Ivy. She releases the change.
On the tablet, My people now includes Grandma Rose, as a picture, in her own words.

scenarios.title: Account deletion hold
scenarios.desc: Deleting an account pauses sign-in and starts a 6 to 12 month recovery window. Ivy's tablet keeps working.

steps.cap: Jess opens Delete my account. The screen says what will happen before anything does.
She taps Delete and must enter her PIN.
A last confirmation. Deleting does not erase: it starts the recovery window.
Her sign-in is paused. Ivy’s tablet keeps working, and the shared log stays.
Seven months later the guaranteed part of the window has ended but recovery is still possible.
She enters her PIN on the hold screen and everything comes back.
